sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, password_hash, role, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: email: unique — login lookup by email (auth service) and seed idempotency check; employee_number: unique — natural key, seed idempotency check; manager_id: direct-report lookups (manager visibility)
table leave_types | fields: code, name, requires_approval, max_consecutive_days, is_paid | pk: code | indexes: code: natural key — seed idempotency check and policy FK lookups

table leave_policies | fields: id, leave_type_code, policy_name, annual_entitlement_days, accrual_period_months, carry_forward_days, min_notice_days, max_request_days, requires_manager_approval, effective_from, effective_to, status | pk: id | fks: leave_type_code -> leave_types.code | indexes: leave_type_code: policy lookup by leave type (balance entitlement/carry-forward resolution); id: seed idempotency check by stable seed id

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start, period_end, entitled_days, used_days, pending_days | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_code -> leave_types.code | indexes: (employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start, period_end): unique — findByKey lookup and seed idempotency check; employee_id: balance reads by employee

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_code, start_date, end_date, requested_days, reason, status, approver_id, approval_comment, submitted_at, decided_at, cancelled_by, cancelled_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_code -> leave_types.code; approver_id -> employees.id; cancelled_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: list/visibility scoping by owner; status: list filtering by state; (leave_type_code, start_date): date-range/type queries; (employee_id, leave_type_code, start_date): seed idempotency composite key — detect already-seeded request and skip
data_notes:
This feature introduces NO new repository interfaces and NO schema changes — it is a development-data seed plus dev tooling. The seed (seeds/ directory, wired into knexfile.js development env) writes directly via the knex instance (the standard knex seed mechanism, not application runtime), so GP-001's repository-pattern rule does not apply to it. The seed must stay column-for-column consistent with the existing repository contracts it populates: PgEmployeeRepository (employees), PgLeaveTypeRepository (leave_types), PgLeavePolicyRepository (leave_policies), PgLeaveBalanceRepository (leave_balances), PgLeaveRequestRepository (leave_requests) — all PostgreSQL via the shared pg Pool. No new repository interface is defined, so the repositories field is intentionally empty.

Seed data contract (binding):
- One manager + one employee, each with password_hash minted by the SAME bcrypt call the auth service verifies with (bcrypt.hashSync(plaintext, 10)); manager_id on the employee points at the manager.
- Leave types + ACTIVE leave policies the balance logic needs (annual entitlement, accrual_period_months, carry_forward_days, min_notice_days, max_request_days).
- One leave_balances row per employee for the CURRENT accrual period (period derived with src/shared/date periodContaining anchored on hireDate — never a hand-written date, preserving the UTC date discipline).
- Two or three leave_requests in different states (e.g. SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED) so list/detail pages have data.
- Idempotency: detect an already-seeded row by composite key and skip (do not duplicate or delete). For leave_requests the composite key is (employee_id, leave_type_code, start_date); for leave_balances it is (employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start, period_end); for employees it is email/employee_number; for leave_types it is code; for leave_policies it is a stable seed id.
- Counter consistency (binding): submitted requests' requested_days appear in the matching balance's pending_days; approved requests' requested_days appear in used_days; rejected/cancelled requests reserve nothing. The seed computes these counters at seed time so available = entitled - used - pending stays correct.

No transaction contract is required: the seed is idempotent and re-runnable, so a partial failure is recovered by re-running (already-seeded rows are skipped, the remainder completes). No runtime multi-step atomic write is introduced by this feature. The seed must never run as part of migrate (it is a separate `npm run seed` step).

transaction_contract: The seed is idempotent and re-runnable (skip already-seeded rows by composite key), so a partial failure is recovered by re-running rather than by a transaction; no runtime multi-step atomic write is introduced. No transaction contract is required for this feature.
